reply.subject: RM_Fuzzrunner

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. South: a nearly spherical ball of grey-brown fur on four short stubby legs, with a small face in the upper middle: rounded ears, pale brows, dark eye bands, a pink-brown nose and long white whiskers. It looks like a raccoon or cat face on a fat rodent. East: a side profile of a long, barrel-bodied, short-legged rodent with a pointed whiskered snout, small rounded ears, a faint dark eye mask and a short fluffy tail. It is lower and longer than the south ball. North: the rear of the ball, with fur, two ear tips over the top, a short pale fluffy tail in the centre and four legs. There is no face. The same grey-buff coat appears on all three.
observed.south.png: A front view of a round, very fat furry animal facing the camera. Two small round ears on top. A narrow face with dark eye stripes, small dark eyes, a pale muzzle and whiskers. The body is almost a perfect sphere and the legs are short and stocky. Painterly fur with soft shading. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A right-facing side profile of an elongated, plump rodent-like body. Rounded ears, a tapered whiskered snout, a dark eye, four short legs with small claws, and a short tufted tail. The silhouette is long and low. Painterly fur. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view: a round furry rump, ear tips showing above, a short cream-tipped fluffy tail at mid-height, and four short legs. No eyes or face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the candidate stands beside the vanilla human and is about a third of the human's height and roughly half a cell long: a small grey rodent on brown ground. In the normal-play inset (32 px/cell) it is a tiny pale-grey blob next to the human and a dark rat, with low contrast against the brown ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face toward the camera: both eyes, the nose, whiskers and both ears, with the body ball behind.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rump and the fluffy tail, with only ear tips above. No eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are ground-level orthographic views showing legs and feet. None is top-down.

SAME_SIZE.seen: South (176 px) and north (170 px) are a tall round ball. East (130 px) is a markedly lower, elongated body. The ear tops and feet in facings.png confirm east is shorter, and its torso is also much less deep than the south ball.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same coat, ears, whiskered face and short fluffy tail on all facings, and the tail turns correctly (rear on east, centre on north, hidden on south). The south ball is rounder than the east barrel, but it is recognisably the same animal.

SIGNATURE.seen: The description's legible physical features, 'round with fog-fat' and whiskers, are present: a very round, fat furry body with prominent whiskers, strongest on south/north.

ALIEN.seen: At first glance it reads as an Earth rodent: a rock hyrax/guinea-pig body with a raccoon-masked face. Nothing in the anatomy (limbs, head, ears, tail, coat) departs from familiar Earth mammals. It is a fat hyrax with no alien feature.

STYLE.seen: Painterly realistic fur and anatomy. Eyes are small and dull, not glossy or smiling. Not cel-shaded, not a photo or 3D render.

OURS.seen: No vanilla or other-mod animal is recognisable. It is consistent with generated in-house painterly art.

ALPHA.seen: Code reports real alpha on all facings. No ground patch, shadow or halo is visible under the feet.

SCALE.seen: About a third of human height at drawSize 0.8: a small common burrow-run animal, which fits the description.

LEGIBLE.seen: In the 32 px/cell inset it is a tiny, low-contrast pale-grey smudge on brown ground. It reads as 'small animal' but has no bold shapes.

findings.seen: A plump grey-brown rodent with rounded ears, a whiskered snout, a raccoon-like dark eye mask and a tufted short tail. A stranger would call it a hyrax, guinea pig or fat raccoon-rodent at first glance. No anatomical feature is alien.
findings.quote: When the card says `earth_body_named: no`, a creature a stranger names as its nearest Earth animal at first glance with the departures bolted on ... is still `STYLE_EARTHLY`.
findings.fix: Give the fuzzrunner an alien body plan that still reads as a round, fog-fat burrow-runner: for example, a low, almost limbless fur-ball with six short legs tucked underneath, no visible snout but a whisker fringe ringing the front, and small sensory pits instead of mammal ears and eyes.

findings.seen: South and north show a tall ball body (176/170 px). East is markedly lower (130 px) and its torso is far less deep than the south ball, so the animal shrinks and changes shape in profile.
findings.quote: Same size on every facing — owner 2026-10-22: "it needs the treatment that makes the different facings the same size."
findings.fix: Draw the east profile with the same body depth and overall height as the south ball, so the side view is as round and fat as the front and rear.

findings.seen: At 32 px/cell it is a tiny pale-grey blob with little contrast against the brown ground.
findings.quote: legibility at 32 px. Both are polish.
findings.fix: Strengthen the outline and the value contrast between the fur and the ground so the round body reads as a bold shape at 32 px per cell.

reply.needs_call_why: The card lists no departures, so the ALIEN test rests on gestalt alone: the creature reads clearly as a hyrax/raccoon-faced rodent. The owner might still accept a 'common little rodent' for flavour. The size spread is partly the ball-versus-barrel body shape, not a pure scale error.
proposals: Give RM_Fuzzrunner a `departures` list on its card (e.g. stone-like stillness texture, whisker fringe, run-polished shoulder pads) so the ALIEN check has concrete features to test instead of gestalt alone.
Could visibly express 'polished by ten thousand shoulders' with worn, sleek shoulder patches in the fur, a defining feature the generator can draw.

reply.image_seen: Image 1 compares three brown-grey furry facings; image 2 shows a round animal head-on with upright ears and whiskers; image 3 shows a low, elongated side profile with four short legs and a tufted tail; image 4 shows rounded haunches and a central tail from behind; image 5 places the side sprite beside a human at game scales.

concerns.evidence: All facings read as a plump rodent: familiar upright ears, dark eyes, tapered whiskered muzzle, ordinary paws and a short furry tail. The round, densely furred body supports the description, but its visible anatomy remains recognizably terrestrial.

On the shared-scale panel, east has a substantially lower back and shallower torso than south and north. All three stand on extended legs without an evident crouch that explains the measured 35% height spread; the tall ball-shaped body becomes a low oval in profile.

findings.seen: The creature reads immediately as a fat rodent, with familiar mammalian ears, muzzle, paws and tail and no clearly alien anatomical structure.
findings.quote: earth_body_named: no — it must not read as its nearest Earth animal
findings.fix: The fuzzrunner retains its round fat reserves and sensory whiskers while showing a coherent alien skull, ear arrangement and limb anatomy that distinguish its silhouette from a terrestrial rodent.
